title: Staged standby cutover and surgical tenant rehome runbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Purpose: Create an operational runbook and automation checklist to perform staged standby cutovers and targeted tenant rehoming during partial cross-region outages. Scope: hosted API + dedicated pools. Excludes private on-prem full air-gap migrations. Background: several recent incidents exposed gaps in combining KV-cache priming, tenant affinity, and VIP level traffic drains. This ticket consolidates playbook steps, automated scripts, monitoring thresholds, communications templates, and a rollback plan. Acceptance criteria: 1) runbook reviewed + signed-off by SRE and Product; 2) playbook automated into one-click orchestration for a single-tenant slice; 3) tabletop drill completes within the 30-minute target; 4) runbook links to dashboards and incident postmortem template.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage & scope: Confirm region(s) impaired via redwood-regions dashboard; identify impacted clusters and tenant slices (tenant IDs). Owner: on-call SRE.
2) Stakeholder comms: Open incident in PagerDuty, tag #infra-escalations, notify account owner(s) using customer-communication-template v2 (Confluence link). Owner: incident commander.
3) Assess KV cache desync risk: Run kv-consistency-checker --region <region> --tenants <list>; if >5% missing prefixes, enable read-fallback to origin store. Owner: storage eng.

4) Prepare standby capacity: Verify warm-standby fleet in candidate region has reserved capacity for tenant classes (priority mapping). Run reserve-staged-capacity --region <target> --units <N>. Owner: capacity eng.

5) Prime KV and embeddings: Trigger async prefix primer job for critical tenants to warm KV and embeddings cache (priming reduces tail latency). Owner: runtime-eng; expected priming time 5-12 minutes per tenant slice.
6) Canary cutover: Redirect 5% of tenant traffic via traffic-router --tenant <id> --to-region <target> --percent 5; monitor 1-minute P95 latency, error rate, and token cost. Owner: network ops.

7) Progressively increase: If canary stable for 10 minutes, increase to 25%, 50%, then 100% with 10-minute stability windows. Abort conditions: P95 > 250ms above baseline, error rate >0.5% absolute increase, KV-miss spike >10%.
8) Post-cutover validation: Run end-to-end smoke tests (generate/chat/embedding) for representative prompts; run billing reconcile check for units consumed. Owner: SRE + product.
9) Customer verification: Notify affected customers with handoff checklist and ask for validation window (15 minutes). Owner: account ops.
10) Close incident: Document timeline, attach metrics, create postmortem with action items within 72 hours. Owner: incident commander.
rollback_plan: If canary abort conditions triggered: immediately revert traffic-router to previous region at current percent (stepwise down 100->50->25->0 in under 5 minutes), mark runbook as 'reverted' and open hotfix ticket.

If KV staleness observed after full traffic move: pause write traffic and trigger synchronous KV resync for affected prefixes; if not resolvable in 20 minutes, revert reads to origin for affected tenants.

If warm-standby capacity unavailable or overloaded: initiate graceful degradation policy (reduce batch sizes, enable strict token limits) and route critical tenants to dedicated fallback pool if policy allows.
Emergency rollback contact chain: on-call SRE -> runtime lead -> head of platform; call tree documented in Confluence and must be followed for edge cases requiring hotpatches.
monitoring_playbooks: dashboards/regional-resilience-overview (P95 latency, error rate, KV-miss % by tenant)
alerts/tenant-tail-latency (alert on sustained 3min P95 > 200ms over baseline)
alerts/kv-consistency-drop (alert when prefix miss rate exceeds 5%)
